title: ROKS TP7 : Lot Turbine
description:
Dans le cadre du projet « ROKS-TP7 Centrale de dotation d'Ova Spin », l'installation de dotation, composée d'un groupe de machines comprenant une turbine, un générateur, une vanne sphérique, la conduite forcée et l'unité de contrôle commande datant de la mise en service initiale en 1968, va faire l'objet d'une révision complète après plus de 50 ans de fonctionnement.


L'objectif de cette révision complète de la turbine de dotation est de la mettre à niveau avec l'état actuel de la technique et de la remettre en parfait état mécanique.

La turbine de dotation a fait l’objet d’une révision partielle pour la dernière fois en 2002.


En résumé, les travaux principaux suivants sont prévus :

- Révision complète du générateur existant. Ce point ne fait pas partie de cet appel d’offres, mais fait l’objet d’un lot distinct

- Révision complète de la turbine avec renouvellement intégral de la protection anticorrosion

- Utilisation de la roue de rechange existante, des aubes directrices de rechange ainsi que d’autres pièces de rechange disponibles

- Enlèvement et élimination des peintures contenant des PCB

- Éventuellement, un nouvel échangeur de chaleur pour l'huile du palier de la turbine

- Remplacement de l’ancienne instrumentation


Caractéristiques techniques de la turbine de dotation :

Turbine Francis horizontale

Marque/type : Bell

Débit d'eau : 0,9 m³/s

Hauteur de chute : 57,64 m

Puissance : 500 kW

Mise en service : décembre 1968

Dernière révision : 2002

Vitesse de rotation : 750 tr/min

title: Belgium – Drilling services – Recompletion of DZH4 – Work-over Rig Services
description: FLUXYS wishes to perform a workover operation on its natural gas storage facility in WUUSTWEZEL (Loenhout), about 30 km from Antwerp near the Dutch border. The subsurface installations of the Underground Gas Storage of Loenhout consist of different types of wells depending on their function and the geological layer they reach: Dinantian Exploitation wells, He1 zone (Cretaceous) monitoring wells, Dinantian Gas Water Contact monitoring wells, Dinantian Peripheral monitoring wells, Namurian monitoring wells, Cretaceous monitoring wells and Eocene monitoring wells. The campaign focuses on one recompletion of a Dinantian Gas Water Contact monitoring well: DZH4. Following a well inspection campaign in 2023, it was found that the well DZH4 was presenting an increased level of corrosion (pittings) on the completion tubings. Therefore 2 recommendations were made: inject corrosion inhibitors in the well similarly to what is made on production / injection wells and replace the completion equipment within a 3-5 years period. FLUXYS has now decided to proceed with these workover operations to change the completion equipment of the well. The preparation and procurement phases of the operations are planned during 2025-2026 with an expected start of operations during Q3 2027.

title: Perusopetuksen iltapäivätoiminnan hankinta Vantaan kaupungille
description: Perusopetuksen iltapäivätoiminnan hankinta Vantaan kaupungille Vantaan kaupungin hankintayksikkö julkaisee osallistumispyynnön dynaamisen toimittajarekisterin perustamiseksi tämän hankintailmoituksen mukaisesti. Tavoitteena on hankkia perusopetuslain mukainen koululaisten iltapäivätoiminnan järjestäminen oppilaille, jotka ovat oikeutettuja käyttämään palvelua. Perusopetuslain (628/1998) 8 a luvun 48 b §:ssä säädetään aamu- ja iltapäivätoiminnan järjestämisestä ja laajuudesta. Ensimmäisen momentin mukaan kunta voi järjestää ja hankkia tämän lain mukaista aamu- ja iltapäivätoimintaa. Jos kunta järjestää tai hankkii tämän lain mukaista aamu- ja iltapäivätoimintaa, tulee sitä tarjota kunnassa toimivien koulujen ensimmäisen ja toisen vuosiluokan oppilaille sekä muiden vuosiluokkien osalta 17 §:n 2 momentissa tarkoitetuille oppilaille kunnan päättämässä laajuudessa. Perusopetuslain (628/1998) 8 a luvussa määritellyn aamu- ja iltapäivätoiminnan järjestäminen on kunnille vapaaehtoista. Toimintaa voidaan järjestää kunnan omana toimintana, ostopalveluna tai avustettuna toimintana. Vantaan kaupunki järjestää iltapäivätoimintaa avustettuna toimintana siten, että perusopetuksen palvelualue koordinoi, ohjaa ja valvoo iltapäivätoimintaa, mutta varsinaisia toimijoita ovat ulkopuoliset palveluntuottajat. Toiminta katetaan vuosittain opetushallituksesta saatavalla valtionosuudella ja kaupungin osoittamalla määrärahalla sekä huoltajilta perittävillä asiakasmaksuilla. Vantaan kaupungin rahoitus koskee ainoastaan iltapäivätoimintaa. Valituksi tulleilla palveluntuottajilla on kuitenkin oikeus halutessaan järjestää aamutoimintaa koulun tiloissa. Tarkempi kuvaus palvelusta liitteellä 2 Palvelukuvaus. Sopimuskausi on määräaikainen ja voimassa neljä (4) vuotta ajalla 1.8.2027 – 31.7.2031. Sopimuksen ehdot on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnön liitteessä 1 Sopimusluonnos. Sopimukseen liittyy mukautettu dynaaminen menettely, joka on kuvattu tarjouspyynnön kohdassa "Menettely".,

title: Belgium – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – CEFTA TRACES NT Maintenance, Expansion and SPS Digital Systems Support
description: Maintenance, support and expansion of CEFTA TRACES NT and related SPS digital systems. CEFTA TRACES NT is a digital platform supporting the electronic processing and exchange of phytosanitary certificates, veterinary health certificates, CHED-like documents, pharmaceutical permits and notifications on non-compliant consignments. The platform supports traceability, information exchange and risk management in the sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) area. The contract will also support interoperability with local systems and relevant international platforms, as well as gradual alignment with the EU IMSOC approach, including TRACES NT, RASFF/iRASFF, EUROPHYT and ADIS-related functionalities, where relevant.

buyer: NHS Coventry and Warwickshire Integrated Care Board
title: Pre Front Door Integrated Urgent Care Services
description:
NHS Coventry and Warwickshire Integrated Care Board (CW ICB) are seeking expressions of interest from suitably qualified and experienced providers for the provision of a comprehensive Pre-Front Door Integrated Urgent Care (IUC) model across Coventry and Warwickshire.

This model requires a single, accountable Lead Provider in each of the two geographical areas:
Coventry (Lot 1) and
Warwickshire (Lot 2)

The appointed Lead Providers will be responsible for the end-to-end design, mobilisation, delivery, clinical governance and continuous improvement of a whole-system urgent care pathway spanning NHS 111 interfaces, GP out of hours, UTC/MIU, ambulance conveyance alternatives, Emergency Department front-door streaming, same-day emergency care, diagnostics, community response and neighbourhood urgent care pathways.

The ICB is not seeking a provider of isolated urgent care components. It is seeking an organisation with the scale, capability, and system leadership to deliver an integrated Lead Provider model. Providers must therefore bring together all interdependent services, healthcare professionals and current Providers, including urgent primary care, community response, and mental health crisis interfaces, into a coherent, accountable and high-performing model.

Contract Length is expected to be 5 years, commencing 1st September 2027 with the Commissioner having the option to extend the Contract for up to a further 5 years.

Further details are provided in VI.3

title: Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR)
description: 1.0 INTRODUCTION The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), PMA-209, located at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland, is seeking information from potential sources regarding a modular Software Defined Radio (SDR) for U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft, designated the Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR). The NGTR is intended to support voice and data waveforms in the Very High Frequency (VHF) and Ultra High Frequency (UHF) bands, with operational capability extending up to 6 GHz. It will incorporate a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) to meet National Security Agency (NSA) cryptographic and Security Evaluation Requirements Document (SERD) requirements. Additionally, the NGTR is designed to serve as a form, fit, and function backwards-compatible replacement for aircraft currently equipped with the ARC-210 Generation 5 and Generation 6 radios. This Market Research tool is being used to identify potential and eligible firms, of all sizes, prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a solicitation. The results of the Request for Information (RFI) will be utilized to determine if any Small Business Set-Aside opportunities exist. Additionally, this RFI is being used to gather constructive information from industry to improve the RFP. The following documents are attached to this RFI Notice: Attachment 1: NGTR RFI Performance Requirements - DRAFT Attachment 2: Program and Risk Feedback Matrix The following dates are anticipated time frames associated with this requirement: Estimated Industry Day: 2nd Quarter FY27 Estimated Draft RFP Release: 3rd Quarter FY 27 Estimated Final RFP Release: 4th Quarter FY 27 Estimated Award Date: 2nd Quarter FY 28 Target Fleet Delivery: Mid-2034 � Production-ready NGTR systems delivered to fleet locations for aircraft installation Primary Place of Performance: Contractor facility and as needed at government test sites and government facilities for meetings with NAVAIR and NSA. 2.0 DISCLAIMER THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS REQUEST IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. 3.0 PROGRAM BACKGROUND The NGTR system's goal is to develop a small form factor system compatible with existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft that will support: Communications waveforms in the VHF, UHF frequency bands with support for waveforms up to 6GHz. Waveforms defined in Attachment 1. A Modular, Open architecture to support rapid capability integration and obsolescence upgrades including a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) that supports NSA cryptographic and SERD requirements. Zero Trust System security meeting applicable Risk Management Framework (RMF) controls. Minimal integration impact and modification requirements for existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft platforms. 4.0 SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS AND REQUIRED CAPABILITIES The NGTR system is expected to meet the performance requirements defined in Attachment 1: �NGTR RFI Performance Requirements� - DRAFT. The NGTR Contractor is expected to meet the following qualifications: Have secure military software defined radios with embedded NSA certified cryptography. Have experience in agile and modular development and testing, incorporating customer feedback throughout the process. Have the ability to obtain Top Secret security clearances for employees and facility within 12 months of contract award, including the ability to support development and test up to the Top Secret level. Have experience in developing and producing UHF and VHF RF radios supporting military and non-military communications waveforms. Has experience in Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE). Have expertise and experience in reducing total life cycle support costs and utilizing predictive maintenance strategies to streamline repair procedures and reduce maintenance downtime. Have experience establishing, maintaining, and documenting a proactive DMSMS (Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages) and obsolescence programs. 5.0 ELIGIBILITY The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 334220 (Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing), with a Small Business Size Standard of 1,250 Employees. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 5821, (Radio and Television Communication Equipment, Airborne). Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size in their capabilities statement. Small business primes may now count �first tier subcontracted� work performed by similarly situated entities as if it were performed by the prime itself. title: Pesulakoneiden toimitukset ja asennukset sekä huoltotoiminnot / VAV
description: Pesulakoneiden toimitukset ja asennukset sekä huoltotoiminnot / VAV Tilaajan tavoitteena on hankkia joustava yhteistyökumppani Vantaalla sijaitsevien VAV-konsernin omistamien kiinteistöjen pesuloiden ja kuivaushuoneiden uusien koneiden toimituksiin, asennuksiin sekä niiden huoltotoimintoihin. Tarkemmin tiloihin ja laitekantaan voi tutustua oheisesta kohdeluettelosta. Tilastojen mukaan pesula- ja kuivaushuoneiden koneuusintoihin liittyviä toimeksiantoja esiintyisi tässä kiinteistökannassa noin 60 kpl / vuosi. Tilastojen mukaan pesula- ja kuivaushuoneiden konehuoltoihin liittyviä vikatarkastus-/korjauksia esiintyisi tässä kiinteistökannassa noin 360 kpl / vuosi, jonka lisäksi Tilaajalla on ennakoivaa vuosihuoltotoimintaa. Sopimus ei sisällä määräostovelvoitetta. Tilaaja ei sitoudu hankintailmoituksessa esitettyihin arvioihin hankintamääristä. Tilaaja pitää erityisen tärkeänä, että pesula- ja kuivaushuoneissa käytettävät koneet huolletaan systemaattisesti ("vuosihuollot"). Lisäksi arjessa esiintyvät muunlaiset vikakorjaukset tehdään ripeästi ja että koneet uusitaan elinkaariajattelu huomioiden kustannustehokkaasti. Uusien pesulakoneiden toimituksissa ja asennuksissa palveluun kuuluu mm.: • Pesula- ja kuivaushuoneiden laitekannan uusiminen Tilaajan kanssa erikseen sopien Pesulakoneiden huoltotoiminnassa palveluun kuuluu mm.: • Laitteiden ennakoiva vuosihuoltotoiminta • Kuivausrummun huoltotoimet vikaantumisissa • Pesukoneen poisto-/tuloputken huollot, virran antoon liittyvien vikojen selvittely ja ohjauspaneelien huolto-/ korjaustoimet • Mankelin erilaiset huolto-/korjaustoimet • Kuivaushuoneen puhaltimien virhetilanteiden hoitaminen Työtilauksiin voi sisältyä myös tarvikehankintoja ja muita työn suorittamiseen liittyviä palveluhankintoja. Tavoitteiden saavuttamisen edellytykset on kerrottu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnön ESPD-lomakkeella, hankinnan kohteen kriteerit -osiossa sekä hankintailmoituksen liitteissä. Hankintapäätöksen tekoperusteena on kokonaistaloudellinen edullisuus pisteytyksen mukaisesti, jossa maksimipisteet ovat 1000 pistettä. Tarjoajan on annettava tarjous kaikista tarjouslomakkeen töistä. Mikäli Tarjoaja ei ole tarjonnut kaikkia tarjouslomakkeeseen eriteltyjä töitä, tulkitaan tarjous puutteelliseksi. Puutteellinen tarjous hylätään. Tarjoajan kannalta huomioitavaa on myös se, että tarjottujen töiden ja hintojen tulee sisältää kaikki tässä tarjouspyynnössä, hankintasopimusluonnoksessa ja palvelukuvauksessa määritellyt kriteerit. Palvelu toteutetaan tarjouspyynnön, palvelukuvauksen ja laatuvaatimusten mukaisesti. Tarjoajan antama tarjous on sitova. Hankintasopimus syntyy vasta kirjallisen sopimuksen allekirjoittamisella, selonottoneuvottelujen jälkeen. EU-kynnysarvon ylittävässä hankinnassa sopimus voidaan tehdä aikaisintaan 14 vuorokauden kuluttua siitä, kun Tarjoaja on saanut tai hänen katsotaan saaneen päätöksen perusteluineen tiedoksi. Tarjoaja ei saa esittää esimerkiksi omissa tarjousasiakirjoissaan ehtoja, jotka vaikuttaisivat hankintasopimuksen sisältöön. Sopimuskauden tavoitealkamisajankohta on 1.4.2027 ja sopimus on voimassa toistaiseksi.,

title: Production of Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (sUAS) Lethality Payloads at Pine Bluff Arsenal
description: 30 OCT 2026 The response due date is 4:00 PM CST on 14 DEC 2026. Submit responses to this request for partnership solutions to debby.c.broyles.civ@army.mil and heather.b.johns.civ@army.mil with subject line: PSO Response Production of Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (sUAS) Lethality Payloads at Pine Bluff Arsenal (PBA). Partnership Solutions Opening � Request for Whitepapers Agency: Department of War (DoW) / Army Materiel Command (AMC) Notice Type: Partnership Solutions Opening (PSO) Title: Production of sUAS Lethality Payloads at PBA. 1.0 INTRODUCTION & AUTHORITY The U.S. Army Materiel Command (AMC) is issuing this request for partnership solutions via white paper submission solely for market research, planning, and concept exploration regarding a potential Public-Private Partnership (P3) under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 7544. The Government is requesting specific conceptual solutions on how to optimally structure and execute P3 Cooperative Arrangements. The core objective is to leverage private investment to modernize Government facilities to Industry 4.0 and 5.0 automation standards. Industry 4.0 is defined as the Fourth Industrial Revolution, is characterized by the "Smart Factory." It aims to create highly efficient, autonomous production lines by integrating cyber-physical systems with the Internet of Things (IoT) and cloud computing. Industry 5.0 is not meant to replace Industry 4.0 but to refine it. It recognizes that pure automation can overlook human creativity and environmental impact. It places the well-being of the worker and the planet at the center of the industrial process. This modernization will enable authorized co-production and facility-use activities that mutually benefit the Government's national security mission and the private partner's commercial enterprise. Disclaimer: This PSO does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), nor is it a procurement action governed by the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR). The Government is not obligated to enter into any cooperative arrangement or agreement because of this PSO and will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with submitting a response. 2.0 PROBLEM STATEMENT PBA is requesting a commercial partnership to support the development and production of lethal energetic payloads for sUAS and Electronic Safe & Arming Devices (ESAD). These efforts include scaling low-cost, modernized sUAS lethality and energetic payload manufacturing. PBA intends for flexible production lines with ability to accommodate modular manufacturing capabilities for differing explosives, varying payload sizes, explosive safe and arming devices, energetic airframes, etc. PBA can provide both logistical and facility support, including approximately 100,000 square feet of storage and production capacity. The government has various 1 or 2 story buildings available in area 34-000 ranging in size from 396 sq ft to 13,551 sq ft with various existing capabilities to include electricity, water, air sewer, Natural Gas, and/or steam. Additional building details provided in Attachment 1. The production facilities were constructed in 1941-42 for the war effort to handle highly volatile chemical, pyrotechnic, and incendiary compounds. Structurally and architecturally, these buildings reflect a combination of standardized strict hazard segmentation, and fortified safety engineering. Buildings are constructed with heavy, reinforced concrete interior blast walls and thick foundations, but with deliberately weak, lightweight exterior walls and roofs. PBA can provide the following support: � Direct labor � Engineering � Base operations � Logistical support � Environmental and safety support, including leveraging PBA's existing Explosive Site Safety Plans to expedite the mandatory joint site-licensing updates required for the partner's specific energetic footprint and, as applicable, for any non-Department of Defense owned toxic or hazardous materials, supporting Government coordination and processing of a 10 U.S.C. 2692 exception request; the contractor remains responsible for providing the technical, environmental, safety, and operational information required to support that request. � Utilities: Existing utility systems vary by facility as shown in Attachment 1. The contractor is responsible for any necessary capital investments required to utilize these utilities, including the procurement and installation of utility meters, sub-meters, service hookups, and distribution lines. 3.0 FINANCIAL & INVESTMENT REQUIREMENTS (CAPITAL EXPENDITURES) To accelerate modernization without requiring upfront Government funding, the selected industry partner(s) must meet the following financial parameters: Private Equity Financed Capital Expenditures (CapEx): An industry partner(s) must utilize private equity or internal corporate capital to fund 100% of the modernization CapEx for the targeted building(s). Scope of CapEx: This investment must cover all necessary facility upgrades, structural modifications, equipment procurement, software integration, and physical installation. Permanent upgrades become Government property upon installation, with the contractor retaining operational use for the duration of the agreement. 4.0 OPERATIONAL CONCEPT: COOPERATIVE ARRANGEMENT In exchange for the capital investment, the Government will enter a Cooperative Arrangement pursuant to 10 U.S.C. 7544(a). Commercial Capacity Guarantee (Facilities Use): In accordance with 10 U.S.C 7544(b)(5), an industry partner will be granted a facilities-use contract guaranteeing a portion of the capacity of the modernized/new lines for their own commercial requirements, with the precise amount to be negotiated based on the overall structure of the partnership, other in-kind considerations offered, etc. Excess Capacity Utilization: Pursuant to 10 U.S.C 7544(c)(3), an industry partner is authorized to use any additional excess capacity not actively utilized or identified for future by the Government. Non-Interference Mandate: As required by 10 U.S.C 7544(c)(2), all commercial production must not interfere with the performance of work for the Department of War. Build-to-Operate (BTO) Model: To accelerate modernization, the cooperative arrangement may utilize a BTO framework. The industry partner will develop, locate, and temporarily operate innovative technological capabilities at OIB sites until they recover their initial capital investment and realize an agreed upon profit. Upon reaching this threshold, operational control transitions to the OIB for long term sustainment, allowing the contractor to refocus on next generation innovation. This BTO model benefits the enterprise by optimizing both sectors' strengths and yields faster capability deployment during the innovation phase and steadier, modernized sustainment production within the OIB. 5.0 MANDATORY STATUTORY PROVISIONS (10 U.S.C. 7544) Indemnification: A selected Industry partner will be required to agree to the indemnity restrictions located at 10 U.S.C. 7544(c)(4). Suspension/Termination: The Government may suspend or terminate commercial activity, or require priority performance for military work, during a war or national emergency. 6.0 PARTNERSHIP PROCESS 6.1 Phase I: Initial Whitepaper Submission Submission: Respondents shall submit an initial written whitepaper addressing the requirements outlined in Section 7.0 (Volumes I, II, and III). Initial submissions must be received within 45 days of the publication of this PSO (no later than 4:00 PM CST on the designated date). Assessment: The Government will assess all timely submissions against the attributes identified in Section 8.0 (Technological Innovation, Financial Viability, and OIB Utilization). 6.2 Phase II: PBA On-Site Visit & Technical Exchange Invitation: The most highly assessed whitepaper respondents will receive a formal invitation detailing the schedule and protocol for a mandatory on-site visit at Pine Bluff Arsenal. buyer: Office fédéral des constructions et de la logistique OFCL
title: (b26054-3) Transformation et rénovation du bâtiment administratif sis Bundesgasse 32 à Berne / CFC 242, 246
description:
La rénovation de l’immeuble sis Bundesgasse 32 permettra de préparer le bâtiment à son prochain cycle de vie et d’adapter certains locaux aux besoins de la Chancellerie fédérale moyennant des transformations limitées. Les travaux de transformation et de rénovation sont prévus de 2027 à 2029, après le départ des utilisateurs actuels.


Conservation des monuments historiques

Le bâtiment fait partie d’un ensemble construit en 1874 et 1875, qui est soumis aux prescriptions relatives à la conservation des monuments historiques applicables à la vieille ville de Berne, inscrite au patrimoine mondial de l’UNESCO. Il sera rénové avec soin, en collaboration avec les services compétents en matière de conservation des monuments historiques. Sa structure sera conservée dans une très large mesure. Les éléments historiques se trouvent principalement dans les étages, dans l’enfilade de pièces située côté sud, et devront faire l’objet d’une attention particulière.


Interventions sur le bâtiment

Les interventions se limiteront à l’adaptation de l’agencement des locaux au rez-de-chaussée, afin d’y créer des espaces polyvalents, et dans les combles, afin d’y aménager des postes de travail modernes et ouverts. Dans les étages, certains bureaux seront regroupés dans la mesure du possible.

Les polluants présents seront éliminés dans les règles de l’art. Les installations techniques du bâtiment et les installations de sécurité ne sont plus conformes à l’état actuel de la technique et seront remplacées. Les installations sanitaires seront également adaptées aux besoins actuels. Un nouvel ascenseur permettra de rendre le 6e étage accessible aux personnes à mobilité réduite.


Les travaux seront réalisés conformément au standard Minergie-Eco, mais sans certification.


Situation en centre-ville

En raison de son emplacement en centre-ville, l’espace disponible pour les installations et la logistique de chantieres très restreint, ce qui nécessite une planification rigoureuse.


Installations de chauffage et de production de froid

L’immeuble sis Bundesgasse 32–36 est alimenté en chaleur par raccordement au réseau de chauffage à distance d’ewb Berne. La station de transfert de la chaleur et le distributeur de chaleur seront conservés et réutilisés. La distribution de chaleur existante sera renouvelée du sous-sol au 6e étage. Au sous-sol, les installations seront adaptées aux nouvelles conditions. De nouveaux radiateurs sont prévus au rez-de-chaussée et au 6e étage. Du 1er au 5e étage, les radiateurs seront déposés, stockés provisoirement puis reposés. Quatre installations de ventilation seront alimentées en chaleur. Une machine frigorifique sera installée sur le toit pour les locaux techniques présentant d’importants dégagements de chaleur. Dans les locaux concernés, cette chaleur sera évacuée au moyen d’appareils de refroidissement à air recyclé.

title: Un lot de stations individuelles et manuelles pour la gravure de métaux et d’oxides
description:
L’EPFL a l’intention d’acquérir un lot de stations individuelles et manuelles pour la gravure de métaux et d’oxides comme équipements plateforme pour son Centre de MircoNanoTechnologie (CMi).

Le CMi est une installation de salles blanches dédiée à la micro/nano fabrication, centrale pour l’ensemble des facultés de l’EPFL, ainsi que pour les industriels locaux (>650 utilisateurs actifs par an). 

Ce lot de stations individuelles sera dédié aux besoins de recherche de pointe en micro et nano fabrication, et plus particulièrement comme étapes clés afin d’assurer et/ou de retrouver des propriétés de surface compatibles avec le domaine. 

Une grande importance sera accordée non seulement à la qualité de chaque station chimique, mais également à leur facilité d’utilisation et en toute sécurité, à leur sécurité liée aux actions de maintenance nécessaires, et à leur flexible mais néanmoins robuste capacité de contrôle des traitements envisagés dans un environnement type R&D.

La proximité, la réactivité du fournisseur, la qualité du support disponible (technique, procédés) ainsi que la disponibilité des pièces de rechange sur le long terme, système de contrôle et logiciels inclus, seront également de grande importance.

title: Karup, Denmark DABS-FEV Laydown Site Construction
description: See Presolicitation Notice Attachment for full details. ---- The United States Army Corps of Engineers Europe District (CENAU) has a requirement to provide a new laydown area including concrete tent pads, gravel bed, site improvements and utility connections for developing base expeditionary airfield resources (BEAR) to beddown personnel (550 pax) using Deployable Air Base System (DABS) sets supporting United States Air Force (USAF) contingency operations. The type of shelter in the standard DABS set is the Alaska Small Shelter System (AKSSS). BEAR assets in the standard DABS set to be accommodated within the beddown area include 72 billet shelters, two (2) latrine shelters, two (2) shower shelters, one (1) laundry shelter, one (1) 550-person kitchen package, four (4) command operations shelters, and three (3) morale, welfare, and recreation shelters. Supporting facilities include site development, utilities and connections (electrical power, domestic water & wastewater), and storm water drainage. As part of this anticipated construction contract, a utilities connection extension (domestic water and wastewater) to the limit of site will be performed through a host-nation-directed sole-source local contractor. The contact information for this contractor will be provided in the solicitation. The completed DABS Laydown Site electrical distribution system will use power provided via DABS generator sets; no electric utility grid connection is required. Primary Facilities to be Constructed: Gravel Bed - ~30,957 Square Meters Supporting Facilities to be Constructed (not all inclusive): Concrete Pads for Tents/Shelters Fencing Utilities

description: PRESOLICITATION NOTICE MULTIPLE-AWARD CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT (MACC) FOR GENERAL CONSTRUCTION SERVICES Solicitation No. 75N99027R00002 The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), National Institutes of Health (NIH), Office of Acquisition and Logistics Management (OALM), Construction, A&E, Facilities and Leasing Office (CAFLO), anticipates issuing a Request for Proposals (RFP) for a Multiple-Award Construction Contract (MACC) to support the ongoing construction, alteration, repair, and maintenance requirements of the NIH Office of Research Facilities (ORF). The resulting contracts will be multiple-award Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) construction contracts. Work will be authorized through individually issued task orders. This acquisition is anticipated to be conducted using competitive negotiated procedures under FAR Part 15. The Government intends to award multiple IDIQ construction contracts under FAR Subpart 16.5. Individual task orders will generally be awarded on a firm-fixed-price basis. The anticipated aggregate ceiling is $3 billion over an eight-year ordering period. Individual construction requirements will be competed through task orders among eligible MACC awardees in accordance with the ordering procedures established in the resulting contracts. The solicitation and resulting contracts will include procedures for adding and removing awardees during that period (on/off ramp). The initial seed-project scope estimated construction magnitude, applicable evaluation factors, and proposal submission requirements will be provided in the solicitation. SCOPE OF WORK Work under the MACC will primarily consist of general construction and may include, but is not limited to, maintenance, repair, painting, alterations, architectural work, mechanical systems, electrical systems, plumbing, heating, ventilation and air-conditioning (HVAC), civil work, earthwork, fencing, structural work, steel fabrication and welding, roofing, building renovations, demolition, new building construction, sustainable construction, design-bid-build, and design-build projects. Individual task orders may include one or more construction disciplines and will vary in size, scope, and complexity. All work will be performed in accordance with the requirements, specifications, drawings, and other documents applicable to each individual task order. LOCATIONS OF WORK The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Office of Research Facilities (ORF) is the steward of NIH facilities and is responsible for the planning, design, construction, acquisition, maintenance and operation of NIH owned facilities, which include campuses in: � Bethesda, Maryland, � Frederick, Maryland, � Poolesville, Maryland, � Research Triangle Park, North Carolina, � The Rocky Mountain Laboratories (RML) in Hamilton, Montana. NAICS CODE AND SMALL BUSINESS SIZE STANDARD The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. The NAICS code and small business size standard applicable to the initial seed project is also anticipated to be NAICS 236220 and $45 million, respectively. ACQUISITION STRATEGY AND ANTICIPATED AWARDS This acquisition will be conducted using full and open competition with reserves for eligible small business concerns. NIH anticipates awarding up to twenty (20) IDIQ contracts, consisting of: Approximately four (4) unrestricted/full-and-open awards; and Approximately sixteen (16) awards under small business reserves. The small business reserves are anticipated to include eligible concerns in the following categories: Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone) Small Business; Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB); Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB); and Participants in the SBA 8(a) Business Development Program. The solicitation will identify the anticipated distribution of the sixteen (16) reserve awards among the applicable small business and socioeconomic categories and will establish the eligibility requirements applicable to each reserve. NIH anticipates approximately four (4) awards in each socioeconomic reserve. Offerors must meet all applicable SBA eligibility requirements for the category under which they submit an offer. BONDING CAPACITY Offerors competing for an unrestricted/full-and-open award shall provide evidence from their surety demonstrating, at a minimum, bonding capacity of: $100 million for a single project; and $300 million aggregate bonding capacity. Offerors competing for an award under a small business reserve shall provide evidence from their surety demonstrating, at a minimum, bonding capacity of: $3 million for a single project; and $10 million aggregate bonding capacity. The solicitation will establish the specific documentation required to demonstrate bonding capacity. Performance and payment bond requirements applicable to individual construction task orders will be established in accordance with the solicitation, resulting contracts, applicable law and regulation, and the requirements of each task order. SMALL BUSINESS ELIGIBILITY AND JOINT VENTURES Offerors seeking an award under a small business reserve must satisfy all applicable SBA eligibility requirements for the applicable reserve category and NAICS code. The solicitation will identify any documentation required to establish an offeror's eligibility for the applicable small business or socioeconomic category. Small business concerns intending to submit an offer as a joint venture must comply with all applicable SBA joint venture requirements, including applicable requirements governing SBA-approved Mentor-Prot�g� relationships. Prospective offerors should consult current SBA regulations and guidance concerning joint ventures and the SBA Mentor-Prot�g� Program at www.sba.gov. CONTRACT CEILING AND ORDERING PERIOD The aggregate maximum value of all contracts and task orders awarded under the MACC will not exceed $3,000,000,000.00 over the entire ordering period. The $3 billion ceiling applies collectively to all MACC contracts and is not a per-contractor ceiling. The anticipated ordering period will consist of one eight-year ordering period. There is no anticipated annual or individual-contractor ceiling other than limitations established by the terms of the resulting contracts and individual task orders. MACC holders will remain eligible to compete for task orders, subject to the terms and conditions of their contracts, until expiration of the ordering period or exhaustion of the aggregate MACC ceiling, whichever occurs first. TASK ORDERS All work under the MACC will be authorized through individual task orders. Individual task orders will generally be awarded on a firm-fixed-price basis and will be separately priced. Each task order will establish the applicable scope of work, specifications and drawings, period of performance, applicable wage determination, bonding requirements, and other project-specific requirements. Task orders may be competed among all eligible MACC holders or restricted to eligible small business MACC holders in accordance with the ordering procedures established in the solicitation and resulting contracts. The anticipated maximum value of an individual task order is $800 million. Eligibility to compete for individual task orders may be subject to project-specific requirements, including required bonding capacity. GUARANTEED MINIMUM The Government's guaranteed minimum under each resulting IDIQ contract will be $1,000. The guaranteed minimum will be satisfied through issuance of a task order. The $1,000 guaranteed minimum is a contractual minimum obligation and should not be interpreted as establishing the minimum dollar value of all future task orders. description: En el marco de las competencias que tiene atribuidas Turespaña ha obtenido la autorización del Consejo de Ministros para licitar la concesión de obra pública del Palacio de congresos de Madrid, en la reunión celebrada el 6 de mayo de 2025. El complejo va a ser objeto de una rehabilitación integral que comenzó ya en 2023 con la obra de remodelación y ampliación del Edificio B para convertirse en la futura sede de Onu-Turismo. La nueva licitación tiene por objeto la concesión de obra pública del resto de inmuebles que integran el complejo. El adjudicatario se encargará de redactar el proyecto de ejecución, realizar las obras y explotar el Palacio de Congresos y su aparcamiento por un plazo de concesión de 40 años a cambio de un canon anual que abonará a Turespaña. El plazo de la concesión es de 40 años, incluyendo una fase de redacción de proyecto de ejecución y obra de 48 meses. El CAPEX es de 105,7 Millones de euros, y la TIR de proyecto de 7,65%. Una vez completados todos los trámites administrativos, Turespaña publicará la licitación en la Plataforma de Contratación del Sector Público y el Diario Oficial de la Unión Europa (DOUE). Predmet zákazky pozostáva z technologickej a stavebnej časti odpojiteľnej jednolanovej obežnej lanovej dráhy s 8-miestnymi kabínami s úrovňovým nástupom, údolnej a vrcholovej stanice vrátane sociálneho zázemia pre pracovníkov obsluhy a súvisiacej inžinierskej činnosti. Súčasťou predmetu zákazky je aj vypracovanie realizačnej dokumentácie, dokumentácie skutočného vyhotovenia stavby v rozsahu potrebnom na kolaudáciu a riadne užívanie stavby, ako aj vypracovanie a odovzdanie prevádzkových predpisov, predpisov pre obsluhu, údržbu, vykonávanie skúšok a technickej dokumentácie elektrických a hydraulických prvkov v slovenskom jazyku. Požadovaná kabínková lanovka musí byt’ nová, nepoužívaná, nerepasovaná (ďalej aj ako „predmet zákazky“). Podrobné vymedzenie predmetu zákazky je uvedené vo Zväzku 3 Opis predmetu zákazky súťažných podkladov.

Termenul limită până la care se pot solicita clarificări la Documentația de atribuire: 14 zile înainte de data limită de depunere a ofertelor, solicitările de clarificări vor fi transmise în S.E.A.P. Entitatea contractantă a stabilit două termene limită în care va răspunde tuturor solicitărilor de clarificare după cum urmează: primul termen - limită este în a 22-a zi înainte de data limită stabilită pentru depunerea ofertelor; al doilea termen – limită este în a 11-a zi înainte de data limită stabilită pentru depunerea ofertelor. Cele două termene de răspuns la clarificări nu afectează dreptul operatorilor economici de a adresa solicitări de clarificări pe parcursul întregii perioade care se scurge de la momentul publicării Anunțului de Participare și până la termenul limită cu 14 zile înainte de data limită de depunere a ofertelor stabilită de către Entitatea contractantă. În funcție de complexitatea solicitărilor de clarificare adresate de către operatorii economici, pentru care răspunsurile ar trebui publicate la primul termen indicat mai sus, Entitatea contractantă și-a rezervat dreptul de a publica răspunsurile la clarificări, respectiv la al doilea termen stabilit în Documentația de atribuire.

title: Poland – Electric buses – Zakup i dostawa 4 autobusów z napędem elektrycznym, niskopodłogowych dla komunikacji pozamiejskiej Gminy Kleszczewo
description: Miejscem realizacji przedmiotu zamówienia jest Zakład Komunalny w Kleszczewie sp. z o. o., ul. Sportowa 3. Przedmiot zamówienia został szczegółowo opisany w załączniku nr 3 do SWZ, stanowiącym integralną jej część. W ramach przedmiotu zamówienia Wykonawca jest zobowiązany również do: 1) przeprowadzenia szkolenia dla minimum 24 (dwudziestu czterech) pracowników Operatora (ZK w Kleszczewie sp. z o. o.) w zakresie bieżącej obsługi oraz minimum 4 (czterech) pracowników Operatora, w zakresie bieżącej obsługi i napraw autobusów zgodnie z zapisami Załącznika nr 3 do SWZ i projektu umowy; 2) udzielenia Zamawiającemu bezterminowej autoryzacji upoważniającej go do wykonywania obsługi technicznej oraz napraw gwarancyjnych i pozagwarancyjnych autobusów, urządzeń i instalacji stanowiących przedmiot niniejszej Umowy na potrzeby wewnętrzne Zamawiającego. Przy czym realizacja ww. napraw przez Zamawiającego w ramach udzielonej autoryzacji jest jego uprawnieniem, a nie obowiązkiem. W związku z tym Zamawiający może każdorazowo powierzyć wykonanie ww. napraw Wykonawcy lub gwarantowi. Szczegółowy zakres udzielonej autoryzacji w zakresie napraw mechanicznych, elektrycznych i powypadkowych będzie określony w oddzielnej umowie serwisowej, uwzględniającej postanowienia zawarte w Załączniku nr 3 i 3a do SWZ (zakres autoryzacji ASO). Umowa serwisowa, o której mowa powyżej zostanie podpisana w terminie podpisania umowy na zakup i dostawę autobusów i będzie stanowiła załącznik do tej umowy, przy czym Wykonawca, zobowiązany jest przedstawić Zamawiającemu projekt zapisów umownych dołączając je do oferty; 3) dostarczenia programu i interfejsu umożliwiającego dokonywanie diagnozy, regulacji i oprogramowania pracy autobusów wszystkich zainstalowanych urządzeń/ systemów/ podsystemów; 4) dostarczenia systemu monitoringu w ramach każdego z autobusów, spełniającego warunki szczegółowo określone w Załączniku nr 3 do SWZ; 5) dostarczenia wymaganej dokumentacji technicznej, koniecznej do przeprowadzania bieżących obsług technicznych i napraw, schematu połączeń elektrycznych pojazdu. Dokumentację techniczno-eksploatacyjną oraz katalogi części zamiennych (katalog części także na CD) w języku polskim oraz katalogi on-line – Zgodnie z załącznikiem nr 3 do SWZ. Autobusy, o których mowa w pkt 1 muszą: 1) spełniać wymagania techniczne określone w załączniku nr 3 do SWZ -OPZ; 2) być fabrycznie nowe, wg definicji z ustawy Prawo o ruchu drogowym z dnia 20 czerwca 1997 r., niskopodłogowe oraz posiadać aktualne świadectwo homologacji typu pojazdu WE wydane zgodnie z ustawą z dnia 14 kwietnia 2023 r. o systemach homologacji pojazdów oraz ich wyposażenia, odpowiadać parametrom techniczno-eksploatacyjnym określonym w obowiązujących przepisach określonych w Rozporządzeniu Ministra Infrastruktury w sprawie warunków technicznych pojazdów oraz zakresu ich niezbędnego wyposażenia; 3) być wyprodukowane nie wcześniej niż jeden rok przed dostawą, nieeksploatowane i nieużywane do badań, testów, prezentacji lub celów o podobnym charakterze; 4) być jednej marki, identyczne pod względem konstrukcyjnym, kompletacji, wyposażenia i kolorystyki (uzgodnionej z Zamawiającym zgodnie z Załącznikiem nr 3 do SWZ), oklejone logotypami Programu Fundusze Europejskie na Infrastrukturę, Klimat, Środowisko 2021-2027 (FEnIKS) (w uzgodnieniu z Zamawiającym). UWAGA: Przedmiot zamówienia musi być zgodny z zasadą DNSH („Do No Significant Harm” – nie czyń znaczącej szkody). o której mowa w rozporządzeniu (UE) 2020/852. Wykonawca zobowiązany jest do stosowania rozwiązań technicznych, technologicznych i organizacyjnych, które nie powodują znaczącej szkody dla celów środowiskowych,w szczególności w zakresie: łagodzenia zmian klimatu, adaptacji do zmian klimatu, odpowiedniego użytkowania i ochrony zasobów wodnych i morskich, ochrony środowiska gruntowo-wodnego, gospodarki o obiegu zamkniętym, w tym zapobieganiu powstawaniu odpadów i recyklingu, zapobiegania i kontroli zanieczyszczeniom powietrza, wody lub ziemi oraz ochrony i odbudowy bioróżnorodności i ekosystemów. Zastosowane materiały, urządzenia i technologie powinny charakteryzować się racjonalnym wykorzystaniem zasobów, ograniczeniem emisji i odpadów oraz trwałością w całym cyklu życia obiektu. Wykonawca udzieli Zamawiającemu pisemnej gwarancji na okres nie krótszy niż: 1) całopojazdowa – minimum 24 miesiące od daty odbioru końcowego, 2) na perforację spowodowaną korozją poszyć zewnętrznych oraz szkieletu nadwozia i podwozia jak również pęknięć konstrukcji szkieletu – minimum 120 miesięcy od daty odbioru końcowego, 3) na powłoki lakiernicze oraz antykorozyjne zabezpieczenie podwozia – minimum 60 miesiące od daty odbioru końcowego, 4) na magazyny energii elektrycznej - gwarancja trwałości i poprawnej pracy – minimum 120 miesięcy od daty odbioru końcowego.
